blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Neolithic Age marked the transition to agriculture, animal domestication, and permanent settlements.
Tools were made of polished stone for sharper edges and higher durability, primarily used for farming and clearing forests.
People lived in permanent villages with mud and brick houses and stored grains for future usage.
Cows, goats, sheep, and dogs were domesticated during this period.
Pottery usage became common, and humans began wearing clothes made from cotton and wool.

blocks.content: The Neolithic Age generally extended from 6,000 BC to 1,000 BC, though the exact time varies from region to region.

The Neolithic Age marked a major transformation in human life, often referred to as the Neolithic Revolution. During this period: - Humans began agriculture. - Animals were domesticated. - People started living in permanent settlements.

blocks.content: Commonly domesticated animals included: - Cow - Goat - Sheep - Dog

items: Agriculture began in the Neolithic Age (frequently tested in SSC exams).
Neolithic tools are distinguished by being made of polished stone rather than raw/unpolished stone.
Invention and common usage of pottery and cotton/wool clothing began in this era.
Humans started wearing clothes made from cotton and wool.
